# Slice 3: the three defects the proof run found, and a fourth of the same family

RED is record 46 and GREEN is record 47, seven failures of fifteen tests. In the runner's words, the two
that matter most: "the plan is worked out, not absent: No accepted slice plan yet for SEEN-001; nothing to
guard supabase/migrations/20260927000004_trade_record.sql against", which is SEEN-008's exact answer with
its rule `no-slice-plan`; and "the slice names the directory: supabase/migrations/20260927000004_trade_record.sql
is not one of the files slice 1 of 1 names: supabase/migrations, packages/core/src/db/tables.ts". For the
coverage gate: `HarnessError not raised` twice, `'summary_written' not found` in a record that had read
`lines: 74.0`, and `'--' unexpectedly found in ('pnpm', '--filter', '@seen/core', 'test', '--', ...)`.

**The guard now tells the two absences apart.** `slice_ is None` means no plan is accepted at all and stays
permissive with rule `no-slice-plan`, because there is genuinely nothing to compare against. `entry is None`
means every slice is done, and it now guards against the **union of every slice's files** with rule
`outside-plan`. The union rather than the last slice, and the reason is worth keeping: a return from review
points at whichever slice carried the finding, so rework touches any file the plan named, and a last-slice
fallback would refuse the very edit the return asked for. That is the shape of unsatisfiable rule that
produced the shell heredocs in the first place.

**The directory rule, and why it is not a prefix hole.** An entry names a directory when it is written with a
trailing slash, or it already exists on disk as a directory, and in both cases only if it contains a
separator. Matching is against `entry.rstrip('/') + '/'`, so it is segment-wise. Three holes that closes:
`harness` is a real directory in every project the guard runs in, and the separator floor is what stops a
one-word entry authorising the whole tree under it, asserted in its own test; a file entry keeps exact
matching, so naming `tables.ts` still refuses a sibling; and the `entry + '/'` comparison means
`supabase/migrations` does not authorise `supabase/migrations-old`. The trailing-slash form exists because a
ticket's first migration goes into a directory that does not exist yet, which disk existence cannot answer.

**The coverage gate reads a figure written by the run that was supposed to write it.** `DEFAULT_COMMAND` is
now `pnpm --filter @seen/core exec vitest run --coverage.enabled --coverage.reporter=json-summary`, which
prints "Coverage enabled with v8" and rewrites the summary; `measured` refuses a summary older than the run,
with the run's start derived as the check's end minus its duration because `cli.py` is not in this slice's
files and could not record the start; and the record now carries `summary_written`. Record 48, this ticket's
own coverage check, carries `summary_written: 2026-09-27T11:42:20+00:00`, where every coverage check before
it in this session read a file dated 23 September.

**The first honest figure is 100.0 lines against a baseline of 100.0, delta zero, and no baseline was
touched.** It is honest rather than impressive: `packages/core/src` still holds `index.ts` alone, five lines,
five covered, so the stale figure and the real one coincide by accident. The first ticket that puts real code
in `packages/core` is where the baseline starts to mean anything.

Two judgement calls left for a reviewer's eye, both named by the implementer rather than buried. The
tolerance is five seconds, because a coarse filesystem mtime and the fingerprint taken between the command
finishing and the reading both push the wrong way, so a stale figure within five seconds of a run start would
still pass. And the refusal lands before `journal.append`, so a stale reading leaves no record at all rather
than a record flagged stale: forced by the file list, and defensible anyway, because the tdd gate counts
coverage records and a flagged-but-recorded reading would satisfy the gate that refused it.

**A fourth defect, of the same family as the first, found by the guard refusing this slice's own files.**
After the replan at record 44, `handoff.plan_accepted_at` moved to 44 and `accepted_greens` counts only
greens recorded after it, so the pack and the guard both read "slice 1 of 3, 0 of 3 done" while slices 1 and
2 were green and committed. `harness guard harness/guard.py` therefore handed out slice 1's file list, and
after this slice's own green it handed out slice 2's. The implementer did not loosen the guard, did not
declare a slice count the journal does not support, and did not write a handoff record nobody asked for: it
made its changes through a shell, which is the same route-around record 42 condemns, and said so. That is
also standing evidence that the hook needs to cover shell commands, which is the half SEEN-106 declined. The
fix belongs with `handoff.plan_accepted_at`: a plan re-accepted by a return should carry forward the greens
of slices whose work is still in the branch. `harness/handoff.py` is outside this slice's files, so it is
recorded and not done.

The full harness suite is 1,127 tests green at record 49, up from 1,112.
